sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Huber Heights, Ohio different?
sections.html:
Huber Heights straddles two counties, Montgomery and Miami, and two school districts, which changes which offices you deal with depending on where your parcel sits. Most homes date from the suburban boom that began in 1956 and later rounds of growth, and a good share are mid-priced houses that appeal to first-time buyers, landlords and investors.

The sections below cover the city's history, Census figures, local zoning and landlord rules, Ohio's disclosure statute and the deed steps at the Montgomery County Auditor.

sections.h2: How did Huber Heights get its start?
sections.html:
Huber Heights grew out of Wayne Township, settled in the early to mid 1800s, and became a city on January 23, 1981. It is named for Charles Huber, the developer who built many of the houses that later made up the city. Suburban building began in 1956, and the city later annexed land in Miami County. A small parcel in Greene County was detached in 2013.

The city covers 22.37 square miles on the northern edge of the Dayton area. The Census Bureau counted 38,101 residents in 2010 and 43,439 in 2020, a 14% jump that was the largest gain in Montgomery County that decade.

Location drives the local economy. The city sits near the junction of I-70 and I-75, has two I-70 exits lined with chain restaurants, and has long been a base for trucking firms. Freight, logistics and manufacturing names in the city include ABF Freight, Dayton Freight, Coca-Cola and Metokote. The city bought the Marian Shopping Center at Brandt Pike and Fishburg Road for $2.8 million for redevelopment, and a Buc-ee's opened in April 2026 as the chain's first Ohio location.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Huber Heights homes?
sections.html:
The median home in Huber Heights is valued at $177,300, and owners live in 70.9% of homes. About 89% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, the steadiest figure among the four cities in this Census release.

Wikipedia reports that in January 2013 an investment firm bought about 1,900 houses from the original developer's family and rents them out, roughly one in every eleven homes in the city. A seller should expect rental competition in some neighborhoods.

sections.h2: Which school districts and services cover Huber Heights?
sections.html:
Two public districts serve the city. Addresses in the Montgomery County part belong to the Huber Heights City School District, which has five elementary schools, one middle school and Wayne High School. Addresses in the Miami County part belong to Bethel Local Schools. Check the county on your tax bill to see which applies.

  • A new public library, a branch of the Dayton Metro Library, serves the city.
  • The Greater Dayton Regional Transit Authority provides bus service.
  • Zoning and code enforcement operate from 6151 Brandt Pike, and the office line is (937) 237-5815.

sections.h2: What do Huber Heights zoning and building rules require?
sections.html:
The city issues zoning permits for new buildings and accessory structures, exterior alterations, room additions, garages, sheds, carports, pergolas, hot tubs and pools two feet or deeper. Each permit has a $30 application fee and is usually issued within about a week.

The city lists items that need no city permit: fences, driveways, uncovered patios, decks, roof repairs, solar panels and interior work. Many of those do need a permit and inspection from the Montgomery County Building Department, which the city uses as its own building authority. Decks, electrical, heating and air, plumbing, roof repairs and solar panels are on the county's list, and the county can be reached at 937-225-4622.

The Code Enforcement Division posts monthly violation reports, so you can see whether your address has an open case. Resolve any open violation before you list. The permits page lists the forms.

sections.h2: What landlord reporting rule does Huber Heights have?
sections.html:
Chapter 192.21 of the city code requires owners of rental property to file a report with the Tax Administrator within 30 days after a tenant moves in, giving the tenant's name, address and telephone number if known. A second report is due within 30 days after the tenant leaves, with the move-out date and a forwarding address. Owners who miss the reports can be fined up to $100 for each unreported tenant.

If you are selling a rental, file any outstanding reports first, then give the buyer's agent the current tenant details. The city's landlord page carries the form. The permits page also has an application for short-term rental information and the hotel tax form.

sections.h2: When does Ohio treat a Huber Heights house as transferred under the disclosure law?
sections.html:
Under R.C. 5302.30, a transfer occurs when the first contract is signed, not when title passes. The disclosure form therefore has to reach prospective buyers before or soon after they commit, and it can go by personal delivery, ordinary or certified mail, or fax.

  • The statute covers sales, land installment contracts, leases with an option to buy and exchanges of one to four unit homes.
  • A transfer in a divorce settlement, to a government body, or of brand-new, never-occupied construction is exempt.
  • A signed acknowledgment from the buyer completes the exchange.

See the full text of the statute.

sections.h2: What does the Montgomery County Auditor require for a Huber Heights deed?
sections.html:
Montgomery County treats a deed transfer through the Auditor as the step that makes the transfer legal. The county charges a mandatory conveyance and transfer fee of $3 per $1,000 of the actual sale price plus $.50 for each parcel. The Auditor's deed transfer line is 937-225-4373, and filings can be made electronically through ePN or Simplifile.

The statement of value that goes with the deed must show the full consideration, including any mortgage the buyer takes on, under R.C. 319.202. Parcels in the Miami County part of Huber Heights go through the Miami County Auditor, so ask that office for its rates and procedure. The county's deed transfer page has the forms.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Huber Heights seller?
sections.html: A direct sale suits owners with a deadline, a tenant-occupied house, or a house with repairs they cannot fund. A listing fits a house in good condition and an owner who can wait for showings and a lender's appraisal. Compare any cash offer with the net from a listing after repairs and holding costs, and read the contract before signing.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Huber Heights deed?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Montgomery County and goes through the Montgomery County Auditor. Parcels in the Miami County portion go through the Miami County Auditor, so check the county shown on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a city permit to replace my roof in Huber Heights?
faqs.a: The city lists roof repairs and replacement as needing no city permit, but the Montgomery County Building Department lists roof repairs among work that needs its permit and inspection. Call 937-225-4622 to confirm.

faqs.q: What happens if a Huber Heights landlord does not file tenant reports?
faqs.a: The city can fine an owner up to $100 for each unreported tenant. Reports are due within 30 days after a move-in and again within 30 days after a move-out.

faqs.q: When is the Ohio disclosure form considered transferred?
faqs.a: R.C. 5302.30 treats the transfer as occurring when the first contract is executed, even if title passes later, so the form should reach buyers early.

faqs.q: Which high school serves a house in Huber Heights?
faqs.a: Wayne High School serves the Montgomery County portion through the Huber Heights City School District. The Miami County portion belongs to Bethel Local Schools, so confirm with that district.
